prompt:
Draft a procedure for design and development of new products at a consumer electronics company. Include design inputs (market requirements, regulatory, standards), design stages with gate reviews, verification methods (simulation, prototype testing, HALT), validation with end users, design transfer to manufacturing, and design change control. Align with ISO 9001 clause 8.3.

Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
- document (string): the complete procedure or document text
- sections (string): structured sections of the document
- clauseRefs (string): ISO clause references addressed

End your response with exactly one line: ANSWER: <your JSON object>
response:
{
  "document": "1. PURPOSE
This procedure establishes a structured process for the design and development of new consumer electronics products in alignment with ISO 9001 Clause 8.3. It ensures that products meet customer requirements, regulatory standards, and quality objectives while enabling efficient transfer to manufacturing and controlled change management.

2. SCOPE
Applies to all new product development activities within the Consumer Electronics Division, including hardware, firmware, and associated software.

3. DESIGN INPUTS
3.1 Market Requirements: Gathered via customer surveys, competitive analysis, sales forecasts, and focus groups. Documented in the Product Requirements Document (PRD).
3.2 Regulatory Requirements: Compliance with FCC, CE, RoHS, REACH, UL, IEC 62368-1, and other applicable regional and industry standards.
3.3 Standards: Adherence to internal design standards (e.g., EMC layout guidelines, thermal design rules) and international standards (ISO/IEC, IEEE).
3.4 Safety and Reliability: Defined via Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and reliability targets (e.g., MTBF > 50,000 hours).
3.5 Input Documentation: All inputs are reviewed, approved, and recorded in the Design Input Register.

4. DESIGN STAGES AND GATE REVIEWS
4.1 Concept Phase: Initial ideation, feasibility assessment, and high-level architecture. Gate Review 1 (GR1): Approval to proceed based on market alignment and technical feasibility.
4.2 Preliminary Design: Schematic capture, block diagrams, material selection. GR2: Review of design architecture, risk assessment, and compliance plan.
4.3 Detailed Design: PCB layout, firmware coding, mechanical CAD, BOM finalization. GR3: Verification of design outputs against inputs; approval to build prototypes.
4.4 Prototype Build: Assembly of engineering samples. GR4: Review of prototype test results and readiness for validation.
4.5 Validation and Finalization: User testing, regulatory certification, design freeze. GR5: Final approval for design transfer to manufacturing.

5. VERIFICATION METHODS
5.1 Simulation: Electrical (SPICE), thermal (CFD), mechanical (FEM), and signal integrity (SI/PI) simulations performed at each design stage.
5.2 Prototype Testing: Functional, environmental, and durability tests per test plans. Includes power cycling, button life, drop tests, and vibration.
5.3 Highly Accelerated Life Testing (HALT): Conducted on engineering prototypes to identify design weaknesses under extreme stress (temperature, vibration, voltage). Results used to improve robustness.
5.4 Verification Records: All test results, simulation outputs, and non-conformances are documented in the Design Verification Report (DVR).

6. VALIDATION WITH END USERS
6.1 Beta Testing: Selected customers receive pre-production units under controlled conditions.
6.2 Usability Studies: Observed user interactions with prototypes to assess ergonomics, interface intuitiveness, and feature adoption.
6.3 Feedback Collection: Structured surveys and interviews conducted; feedback logged and analyzed.
6.4 Validation Report: Summarizes user satisfaction, identified issues, and corrective actions. Must be approved before GR5.

7. DESIGN TRANSFER TO MANUFACTURING
7.1 Documentation Package: Includes final schematics, PCB Gerbers, BOM, assembly drawings, test procedures, and quality control plans.
7.2 Process Validation: Run at manufacturing site to confirm yield, cycle time, and defect rates meet targets (PPAP Level 3).
7.3 Training: Manufacturing and QA teams trained on new product assembly and inspection procedures.
7.4 Transfer Approval: Signed off by Engineering, Manufacturing, and Quality Management.

8. DESIGN CHANGE CONTROL
8.1 Change Request (CR): Initiated via electronic form detailing reason, impact, and proposed solution.
8.2 Impact Assessment: Cross-functional team evaluates effect on design, cost, schedule, compliance, and supply chain.
8.3 Approval: Changes require sign-off by Design Manager and Quality Representative.
8.4 Implementation: Updated documentation, revised BOM, and re-verification as needed.
8.5 Communication: All affected departments notified; change log maintained in the Design Change Register.
8.6 Retrospective Review: Monthly audit of change effectiveness and root cause analysis for recurring changes.

9. RECORDS
All design and development records (PRD, DVR, Validation Report, Change Register, GR approvals) are retained for minimum 10 years per ISO 9001 requirements.

10. RESPONSIBILITIES
- Product Manager: Owns PRD and market inputs.
- Design Engineering: Executes design stages and verification.
- Quality Assurance: Ensures compliance and audit readiness.
- Manufacturing: Validates transfer and process capability.
- Regulatory Affairs: Ensures compliance with standards.

11. REFERENCES
- ISO 9001:2015 Clause 8.3
- IEC 62368-1
- FCC Part 15
- RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU
- Company QMS Manual, Section 8.3",
  "sections": "1. PURPOSE
